item.title: Grid Deck 3-Runner AS/RS Pallet
item.description:
Best fit

The open grid deck reduces material weight and supports airflow, drainage and easy visual inspection. Three continuous runners create stable contact on rack beams and common conveyor arrangements, while four-way entry keeps forklift handling flexible.

Configuration options

  • Steel tubes in the deck and/or runners to manage rack deflection
  • Anti-slip plugs, edge lips and identification areas where the mold permits
  • Custom color, molded logo, screen printing or sequential marking
  • Sample and drawing confirmation for conveyor, shuttle and stacker-crane interfaces

Engineering note

Published loads are temporary market-reference values, not a universal rating. Final capacity depends on temperature, load distribution, support span, steel-tube configuration and test method. Confirm every AS/RS application against the approved drawing and test agreement.

item.title: Solid Deck 3-Runner AS/RS Pallet
item.description:
Best fit

The closed deck is designed for applications that value easy cleaning, spill control and a continuous load surface. Integrated anti-slip pads improve carton and container stability, while the three-runner base supports rack beams and powered conveyor sections.

Configuration options

  • Anti-slip pads on the deck as standard for this family
  • Optional deck and runner steel tubes for defined rack spans
  • Custom colors, logo, printing and traceability marking
  • Perimeter lips, drainage details or RFID zones where the selected mold permits

Engineering note

Reference loads are temporary placeholders. Actual performance varies with mold, temperature, support condition, load distribution and reinforcement. The approved data sheet and test method take precedence for every order.

item.title: Reinforced Solid Deck 3-Runner Pallet
item.description:
Best fit

This family starts from the solid three-runner concept and adds a higher reinforcement envelope for demanding unit loads, wider support spans and long service cycles. It is intended for projects where deflection management and repeatability are more important than minimum pallet weight.

Configuration options

  • Multiple steel-tube layouts through deck and runners
  • Anti-slip pads for improved unit-load stability
  • Custom color, marking, molded logo and identification features
  • Pre-production interface and sample review for automated handling systems

Engineering note

“Heavy duty” does not replace project verification. Final rack capacity must be confirmed against the exact support span, temperature, dwell time, load distribution and steel layout. Values shown here are market-reference placeholders.

item.title: Grid Deck Full-Perimeter AS/RS Pallet
item.description:
Best fit

The full-perimeter base provides continuous bottom contact for stable stacking and can improve compatibility with selected conveyors, pallet stops and rack-support arrangements. The grid deck keeps the platform ventilated and easier to inspect.

Configuration options

  • Optional steel tubes to control deck and base deflection
  • Anti-slip components, edge details and identification areas where supported
  • Custom colors, printing, logo and fleet marking
  • Drawing review for conveyor rollers, chain conveyors and support rails

Engineering note

Reference values are temporary. Final capacity depends on the selected mold, temperature, loading pattern, support span and reinforcement. Always use the approved project specification for purchase and operation.

item.title: Rack Load Is Not a Single Number
item.description:
A rack-load value only becomes meaningful when its test conditions are known. Two pallets carrying the same mass can deflect very differently if the rack beams are farther apart, the load is concentrated, or the warehouse operates at a higher temperature.

Define the support condition

Record the clear span, beam width, contact position and whether the pallet is supported by two beams, rails or a shuttle platform. A drawing is more reliable than a generic phrase such as “used on rack.”

item.title: How to Specify a Pallet for Conveyors and Shuttles
item.description:
Automated handling depends on repeatable interfaces. Start with conveyor type, roller or chain pitch, pallet travel direction, transfer points and locator geometry.

Check the bottom pattern

Runner positions must maintain stable contact throughout movement. Confirm that openings, ribs and steel tubes do not conflict with chains, rollers, stops or lifting elements.

Check sensing and centering

Share sensor position, expected target surface and any centering mechanism. Color and surface geometry can affect optical detection.

item.title: When Steel Reinforcement Adds Value
item.description:
Steel reinforcement is most valuable when it responds to a defined bending direction and support condition. More tubes do not automatically mean a better system.

Start from the load path

Map where the unit load enters the deck and where the rack, conveyor or shuttle supports the base. Tubes should strengthen the span that actually bends.

Balance stiffness and handling

Additional steel increases pallet weight and can affect manual handling, shipping density and corrosion requirements. Select tube quantity and coating as part of the full operating environment.

item.title: Can all four pallet families add steel tubes?
item.description: Yes. Grid three-runner, solid three-runner, reinforced solid three-runner and grid full-perimeter pallets can all be configured with steel tubes. Available quantity and position depend on the selected mold.

item.title: Can we test a sample before a bulk order?
item.description: Yes. For AS/RS projects, sample confirmation is strongly recommended. Please provide interface drawings and test conditions so the sample represents the final application.

item.title: Can you customize color and logo?
item.description: Yes. Custom colors, molded logos, printing and identification marks can be discussed. Minimum order quantity and color tolerance are confirmed with the quotation.

item.title: How do we confirm rack load?
item.description: Rack load must be confirmed with the exact pallet model, support span, temperature, dwell time, load distribution and steel-tube layout. We recommend an approved drawing and representative sample test before mass production.

item.title: What information should we send for a quotation?
item.description: Please send pallet dimensions, unit-load weight and distribution, rack or equipment support details, entry direction, operating temperature, required quantity, color and any marking requirements.

item.title: What material do you use?
item.description: The current product range is injection molded in HDPE. The exact material grade and any special temperature, hygiene or recycled-content requirements should be confirmed for each order.

item.title: High-Bay Warehouse with Long Rack Dwell Time
item.description:
For a high-bay warehouse storing boxed goods, the main risk was long-term deflection across a defined beam span. A reinforced solid three-runner platform was shortlisted for its continuous deck and expanded tube options.

The confirmation plan included load-distribution drawings, steel layout, maximum dwell time and a sample rack test. Conveyor transitions and sensor targets were checked before the pallet specification was frozen.

This is an illustrative project scenario. Replace it with verified customer details when available.

item.title: Ventilated Pallet for Automated Cold Storage
item.description:
A grid three-runner pallet was considered for a cold-storage flow requiring drainage, visual inspection and four-way forklift access. The project review focused on low-temperature material behavior, rack span and anti-slip requirements.

A representative sample was conditioned to the operating temperature and tested across rack and conveyor interfaces before approval.

This is an illustrative project scenario. Replace it with verified customer details when available.

item.title: Full-Perimeter Base on a Mixed Conveyor Line
item.description:
A mixed conveyor line used rollers, chains and mechanical stops. The full-perimeter base offered a broader contact pattern, but runner positions and transfer clearances still required drawing review.

The team mapped every transition, confirmed entry direction and ran a loaded sample through the critical points before production.

item.title: Disclaimer
item.description:
All product loads, dimensions, weights and configurations shown on this website are preliminary reference information. Performance depends on the selected mold, material grade, steel reinforcement, temperature, load distribution, support span, dwell time and test method.

Do not select a pallet for an AS/RS solely from website values. The final approved technical data sheet, drawing, sample validation and commercial agreement take precedence.
